rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a compositional change (partial substitution of Mo with Nb), whereas the hidden target uses thermomechanical processing (cold rolling and annealing) on a specific non-equiatomic alloy. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies room-temperature compression testing on cast/annealed alloys, while the target uses room-temperature tensile testing on cold-rolled and annealed material. The testing mode (compression vs. tension) and processing history differ, placing them in different broad regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes reduced electronegativity difference and lattice bond heterogeneity to enhance dislocation mobility, while the target's mechanism relies on work hardening, dislocation accumulation, texture, and subsequent recovery/recrystallization. These are different classes of mechanisms.

The target reports changes in tensile strength and elongation with rolling/annealing, starting from a much lower baseline strength (1007 MPa tensile). The predicted property direction and magnitude are not aligned with the target's outcomes.
